page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Falsv7 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor. This configuration features 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, operating at a high base clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage, though it is premium storage capable, and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the high-frequency AMD processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, however, falls into the average range, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register average performance. For specialized workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small language models, but drops to the bottom 25% for prompt processing on medium 7B models, highlighting a performance tradeoff when handling larger memory-bound tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F4als_v7 offers a high-frequency compute profile with a low memory footprint, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory allocations. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs keeps the baseline resource cost aligned strictly with CPU capabilities. This hardware profile is suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic computational workloads such as small-scale simulations or microservices.

This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, low-memory workloads, making it suitable for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, and microservices.
